prompt: explain how greenhouse gases warm the Earth

keyLinks.effect: It passes through the atmosphere and warms the surface
keyLinks.mechanism: The atmosphere is largely transparent to incoming sunlight

keyLinks.effect: The surface gives off heat as infrared radiation
keyLinks.mechanism: Every warm object radiates energy; Earth's temperature means infrared

keyLinks.cause: Infrared travels up through the air
keyLinks.effect: Greenhouse gases (CO2, water vapour, methane) absorb it
keyLinks.mechanism: These molecules absorb infrared wavelengths that other air molecules let through

keyLinks.effect: They re-emit it in all directions, including back down, so less heat escapes to space
keyLinks.mechanism: Absorbed energy is re-radiated, part of it toward the surface

keyLinks.cause: More greenhouse gas means less heat escapes
keyLinks.effect: Earth warms until it again sends out as much energy as it receives, at a higher temperature
keyLinks.mechanism: Energy balance: outgoing must match incoming

keyLinks.effect: More water vapour or less ice, which adds more warming (reinforcing loop)
keyLinks.mechanism: Warmer air holds more water vapour; less ice reflects less sunlight

knownErrors.claim: The ozone hole lets in extra heat and is the cause of global warming
knownErrors.why: Ozone depletion and the greenhouse effect are different problems

knownErrors.claim: Greenhouse gases trap the incoming sunlight
knownErrors.why: They mainly absorb the outgoing infrared from the surface, not incoming visible light

knownErrors.claim: Heat bounces off a solid layer or glass-like ceiling in the sky
knownErrors.why: Gases absorb and re-emit infrared; there is no reflecting layer (a blanket analogy is fine)

knownErrors.claim: Without greenhouse gases Earth would have about the same temperature
knownErrors.why: The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth roughly 30 °C warmer than it would otherwise be

acceptableSimplifications: A blanket analogy for the atmosphere
Omitting the exact gases other than CO2
